## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c41e2768d34596930bd8076a40993328b1763412`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #37562 (body, triage, claim, os-dev-report), PR #37646 (body, 3 files), the net diff `origin/main...c41e2768d3`, the cited code on the head (`packages/spec/src/ai/record-body-anchor.ts`, `ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/MarkdownContent.tsx`, `sanitizedHtml.tsx`, `plugin-detail/src/DetailSection.tsx`), and the head's check-runs: 38 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure (Test UI 16/16, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check · debt ledger all success).

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept sets: none touched. No `packages/**`, no schema, no governed path; the diff is one UI module, its test and a changeset, inside the claim's file surface. Right.
- Public surface: none. `@object-ui/app-shell` is `private: true`, and `recordSectionAnchor.ts` is not re-exported from its index (its only consumer is `RecordDetailView.tsx`). `SectionCandidate.unlisted` (required) and `SectionTarget.fieldOnly` (optional) are internal-only. `stripBodyTags` and `BodyHeading` are consumed from `@objectstack/spec/ai` as published on `main`, not changed. Right.
- Behaviour: the count guard is now `unlisted === 0 && drawn.length === count`. An empty reading, like a `textarea`, is `fieldOnly` and scrolls as soon as the field is drawn. Both match the card's N6 and N7.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix) — The markdown scan misses shapes that draw a same-titled heading. The guard is only sound if `unlisted` over-counts: every drawn heading outside the outline has to be counted, and a miss is exactly the N6 defect. The missed shapes, against `react-markdown` 10 + `remark-gfm` (the field's face):
  - (a) a setext heading inside a quote (`> Scope` over `> ---`). `isSetextUnderline` sees the leading quote marker and refuses the line, though the PR does handle ATX behind a quote.
  - (b) a setext heading whose paragraph follows, with no blank line between, a line that is not paragraph content: an HTML comment line, a link reference definition, or an indented code line after a blank. The joined text then reads `xscope`, not `scope`.
  - (c) an ATX heading in a GFM footnote definition (`[^1]: # Scope`), and the `Footnotes` label h2 that remark-gfm draws for any body with footnotes.

  Each of these, together with one listed-but-undrawn same-titled heading, still marks the wrong section. The fix: run the container-prefix walk (`containedAtxText`'s) before the setext test. Reset or skip the paragraph on comment, reference-definition and indented-code lines. Count a footnote definition's ATX and the `Footnotes` label. Add one test row per shape. Narrow reach, and strictly better than `main` (no regression in the unsafe direction), so it is not a must-fix. Take it in this PR or on a follow-up card.
- N1 (nit) — Some shapes are counted but never drawn by this face:
  - a raw heading-tag line in a markdown body (no `rehype-raw`, and `rehype-sanitize` drops raw nodes, so no heading element is drawn);
  - a 4-plus-space `    # Scope`;
  - a lazy `> Scope` over `---`.

  They err in the safe direction, as the PR's Acceptance notes say. But a body that `main` marked correctly now opens the field, and only after the 4 s settle (see N3). The shape test's title ("every place a face draws") pins the raw-tag row as drawn, which is wrong for this face. Reword it.
- N2 (nit) — This one is older than the PR and outside N6 as the card words it. The outline reads a markdown heading's source, so `# [Scope](#x)` reads `scopex` and `# Q & A` keeps `amp`. The face reads the rendered text. A listed heading that is drawn under the cited reading is skipped by `listed.has(start)` and counted nowhere, which gives S1's wrong-section result. Note it on the S1 follow-up if one is filed.
- N3 (nit) — `unlisted > 0` is known from the body alone, so by N7's own logic that target is `fieldOnly` and could scroll at once. This is the dev's out-of-scope note; see seat question 5.

Seat questions:

1. The list is close but not right in both directions. Missed (it draws a heading but is not counted): S1 (a), (b) and (c). Counted but never drawn: N1's three shapes (raw heading-tag lines in markdown, indented code, a lazy quote over `---`). Fenced code is excluded as the spec's outline reader excludes it. That includes its quirks: a ``` line closed by `~~~`, an inline triple-backtick line that toggles, and quoted fences are not seen. The html half is right: every drawn hN comes from an `hN` opener that DOMParser keeps, and unclosed and nested openers are counted as the browser draws them.
2. Holds, as a rule. With `unlisted` a superset of the drawn unlisted headings, `unlisted === 0` means the drawn ones are a subset of the listed ones, so `drawn.length === count` means every listed one is drawn and `ordinal` indexes the right heading. When `unlisted > 0`, `locateSection` returns no heading, and `focusRecordSection` scrolls to the field at the settle. It never marks a heading. Its soundness is only as good as the scan, so S1 is where it still fails.
3. Holds. `reading === ''` and `textarea` return `fieldOnly: true`, and the `attempt` branch scrolls at once through `scrollTo`. A titled heading not yet drawn returns a plain `{ field, face }` and waits for the timer. The `scrollTo` wrapper that calls `mayScroll` is unchanged in the diff. `RecordDetailView.citedSection-37365.test.tsx` (the S5 pins) is untouched, and Test UI is 16/16 green on the head.
4. Yes, they are real controls, read from the code. N6 ablation: without the `unlisted` term, the combined body draws 2 against a count of 2, so `drawn[0]` (the setext heading) is returned and `heading toBeUndefined` goes red. The paragraph-line control marks `atx`, so the guard does not just open the field every time. N7 ablation: `face === 'text'` gives no immediate scroll, so `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` goes red. Its control (`Intro` waits until the timers advance) would go red for a mutation that scrolled every field at once. The 1-failed-of-21 runs come from the dev's report only. Per the brief they were not re-run.
5. Fine as recorded. It is a latency and not a correctness defect, and it is the behaviour that a count mismatch already had on `main`. One caveat (N1): the PR's own over-counting moves bodies that `main` marked correctly onto this path, so the fix (`unlisted > 0` then `fieldOnly`, one line) is worth folding into any S1 rework. Otherwise it does not need its own card.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/37562-section-locate-edges.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. The level is right: a private package, a behaviour fix with no public surface change, Check Changeset success.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset, as the card's Acceptance requires. Right: no accept set widens or narrows.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none were raised.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (the settle wait when a same-titled place is outside the outline): answered in seat question 5 and N3. Fine as recorded.
- Deviations:
  - Base `b1c41e55e`, not the premise's `4e10d4bff`: the views directory has no diff between the two. Fine.
  - Full app-shell suite not run locally: CI Test UI 16/16 carries it. Fine.
  - `check:type-check-debt`: the PR body says NOT MEASURED, while the later report says it was re-run, exit 0. CI `Type Check · debt ledger` success settles it.
  - Commit-trailer and footer deviations: they follow the dispatch. Fine.
- Security: none. Both new scans are forward scans with no backtracking pattern. The html searches stay monotonic, and each segment between openers is scanned once.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. This is client-side text and DOM matching, with no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `c41e2768d34596930bd8076a40993328b1763412`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5

1. **Shape**: draft against `main`. `recordSectionAnchor.ts`, its test and a patch changeset, +256/−21. Not governed, not security-touching. `Clause-②: no` is right (`@object-ui/app-shell` is private).
2. **Premise**: counting the places outside the outline that could draw a same-titled heading, and trusting the ordinal only when that count is 0, is the right rule. N7 holds: an empty reading scrolls when the field is drawn, the `mayScroll` contract is unchanged, and the S5 pins pass.
3. **Gates**: contract record 7200419777 (`TIER_DEFAULT`) reads PASS, with one should-fix owed. CI on this head: 0 failed.
4. **Owed before landing**:
   - **S1**: the hand-written line scan misses headings the field's renderer draws, such as a setext heading inside a quote, a setext heading under a comment, a link definition or indented code line with no blank line, and headings inside a GFM footnote, including remark-gfm's own "Footnotes" h2. It also counts some that it never draws (N1). The seat's ruling on the route: stop scanning lines for the markdown half. Count headings from the same parse the renderer uses (remark with remark-gfm, the field's pipeline), so the count matches what is drawn by construction. That closes S1 and N1 together. Keep the HTML half. Pin S1's shapes and N1's shapes as cases.
5. **Ride along**: N3 (a non-zero unlisted count already answers from the body, so open the field at once rather than after the 4 s settle; a one-line change). N2 is older than this PR: file it as a p3 follow-up under #37562 (the outline reads source text, the page reads rendered text).
6. **Landing terms**: after the delta, the same reviewer re-checks it. Then the area lands it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c3f7728e8e1e8936502601e58c22b21980bcc96b`
Local-runs: none

Delta review over the earlier record on `c41e2768d3`, after seat REWORK 7200445298.

What I read:
- the delta `c41e2768d3..c3f7728e8e` (3 commits, 9 files) and the net diff against `origin/main`;
- the PR body and both changesets;
- claim amendment 7200539429 and os-dev-report 7201722157;
- #37664 (N2's follow-up, open);
- the check-runs on the new head.

Every check-run on the new head has concluded, with none failed. The `Check Changeset` re-run that followed the body edit to `Clause-②: yes (widening)` concluded success at 19:35Z. Test UI (all planned shards), Build & E2E UI (the ineffective-dynamic-import ledger), Type Check UI, Lint UI, Lint & Repo Gates and Governed Surface Queue Guard all passed.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept sets: none touched. No `packages/**`, no schema, no governed path. The file surface widened to `ui/packages/fields` under claim amendment 7200539429, and the diff stays inside it. Right.
- Public surface: `@object-ui/fields` gains exactly two exports from its index, `loadDrawnMarkdownHeadings()` and the `DrawnMarkdownHeading` type.
  - The new constants `MARKDOWN_REMARK_PLUGINS`, `MARKDOWN_REHYPE_PLUGINS` and `drawnMarkdownHeadings` are reachable only through the internal `MarkdownContent.js` module. The package `exports` map has no subpath for it, so they are not public.
  - The index only re-exports the type from `markdownHeadings.ts`, and that import is erased, so react-markdown stays in the lazy chunk. The dev's local build reads +297 B gz on the eager closure, with no new eager chunk.
  - Additive. Right.
- `SectionCandidate.unlisted` widens to `number | undefined`, inside private `@object-ui/app-shell`. Not public. Right.

Prior findings:

- S1 — **closed.** The markdown half no longer scans lines. It counts the headings drawn by `drawnMarkdownHeadings`, which runs react-markdown with the same plugin constants `MarkdownContent` now draws with. The reader reads the tree after the last rehype plugin. react-markdown's later `post` step changes no heading here, since the document face passes no `allowedElements`, `skipHtml` or `components`. Every S1 shape is pinned, both against the reader and against the face's own DOM:
  - the setext heading in a quote;
  - the setext heading under a comment, under a link definition and under indented code;
  - the ATX heading in a footnote, and the `Footnotes` label.
- N1 — **closed.** A raw heading tag, an indented code line, a lazy quote over a rule and fenced code now count 0. Each is pinned against the face's DOM (`markdownHeadings-37562.test.tsx`) and as an app-shell row.
- N2 — **stays open, off this PR.** It is filed as #37664. As the PR's Acceptance notes say, the start comparison already turns N2's wrong-section half into a field for this guard. A listed heading drawn under the cited reading is not in `listedAt`, so it counts as unlisted.
- N3 — **closed.** `(unlisted ?? 0) > 0` is `fieldOnly` in `locateSection`'s first condition, so the field is scrolled to at once. The N3 fake-timer case has a control (an undrawn titled heading still waits). The S5 integration test changes only a comment.

New findings:

- N4 (nit) — The two pipelines share their plugin lists, not their options. Any later react-markdown prop added to `MarkdownContent`'s document face (`allowedElements`, `skipHtml`, `components`) would not reach the reader. The divergence test (`drawnByFace` against `texts`, per shape) would notice only for the shapes in its corpus. Exporting one options object that both read would make agreement hold by construction rather than by corpus. It does not block: today the two read the same tree.
- N5 (nit) — `MarkdownContent.tsx` now re-exports non-component values, which adds two `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings at warn level. In dev, a change to that module triggers a full reload instead of fast refresh. This is the cost of keeping one lazy markdown module, which avoided the INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT caught on `6ef69f4f25`. Accepted as recorded.

Coordinator's checks:

1. **Same pipeline?** Yes, as far as the tree goes. `MarkdownContent` passes `MARKDOWN_REMARK_PLUGINS` and `MARKDOWN_REHYPE_PLUGINS` from `markdownHeadings.ts`. The reader calls the same sync `Markdown` with those lists plus one tree-reading plugin appended last. The record page draws the `document` face (`inGridColumn` false), the one the reader matches.

   Is there a test that fails if they diverge? Yes, over a corpus: each S1 and N1 shape asserts that the reader's texts equal the headings `MarkdownContent` draws in the DOM. `start` offsets are pinned, so the sanitizer is shown to keep `position`. The index loader is pinned to resolve the same function. The residue beyond the corpus is N4.
2. **Published, exports, level.** `@object-ui/fields` is published (`publishConfig.access: public`, 18.6.0, in the changeset `fixed` group). The new exports are additive.

   The `@object-ui/fields` changeset is `patch` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. AGENTS.md (Definition of done §3) says a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`. Right.

   `@object-ui/app-shell` stays `patch` with `Clause-②: no`. That is private and right. The PR body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line-initial, and Check Changeset is success on that body.
3. **The window before the reader resolves.** It never marks or scrolls to a wrong heading.
   - A pending markdown candidate has `unlisted: undefined`. `(undefined ?? 0) > 0` is false, so it is not `fieldOnly`, and `counted` needs `unlisted === 0`, so no heading is returned. `attempt` does nothing, and the only possible move is the settle timer scrolling to the field.
   - Once the reader resolves, `current` is re-counted through the `pendingUnlisted` WeakMap. `RecordDetailView` passes the memoised candidate objects themselves, so the keys hold. Then `attempt` runs.
   - If cleanup or the settle came first, `done` makes it a no-op. A failed load resolves with the reader still unloaded, so the candidates stay untrusted and the field opens at the settle. No unhandled rejection; the next call retries.
   - The fresh-module case (`vi.resetModules`) pins "no heading before load, marked and scrolled once after". The failed-load branch has no test, and it is too small for that to be a finding.
4. **Same title twice inside the outline.** Holds.
   - `listedAt` holds the starts of every listed heading of the cited reading. `headingsOf` lists only column-0 ATX lines, and its `start` is that line's offset, CRLF included. The mdast heading position for a column-0 ATX is the same offset. A column-0 ATX can never be a lazy continuation inside a container, so both listed duplicates match their drawn starts and `unlisted` stays 0.
   - Then `drawn.length === count` and `ordinal` picks the right one. The existing `scope` / `scope-2` cases still pass.
   - If one duplicate is undrawn (in an HTML block), `drawn.length` is less than `count`, and the field opens at the settle. That is safe.
   - Footnote headings are never at column 0 in the source, so they are always unlisted. That also covers their DOM order differing from source order.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/37562-fields-drawn-markdown-headings.md`: `'@object-ui/fields': patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right (see check 2).
- `.changeset/37562-section-locate-edges.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, with its body updated for the parse-based count. Right.
- PR body: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial. This review's face is the declaration face, and `TIER_DEFAULT` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none.
- Rework items: S1 and N1 (the route ruling), N3 and N2 are each answered above.
- Dev deviations:
  - The full fields suite was taken on `6ef69f4f25`, and the four targeted files were re-run on the head. CI Test UI on the head carries it. Fine.
  - The PR body write was left with the seat, and the body now on the PR carries the final declaration lines. Fine.
- Eager closure: +297 B gz with no new eager chunk, from the dev's reading. CI Build & E2E UI is green on the head.
- Security: none. The sanitizer still runs inside the reader, and the reader only reads text and offsets.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. This is client-side markdown parsing and DOM matching, with no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37562-section-locate-edges`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**
